newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weak Japan M2+CDs due to fewer loans--economists.
newsitem.headline: Weak Japan M2+CDs due to fewer loans--economists.

text.p: Weak growth in Japan's money supply in June was largely due to sluggish demand for bank loans, economists said on Thursday.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) said earlier that Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (CDs) grew a preliminary 2.8 percent in June from a year earlier.
M2 plus CD growth for May was revised up to 3.1 percent from a preliminary 3.0 percent.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected the June figure to rise by 2.8 percent to 3.1 percent year-on-year. Most had forecast a rise of either 2.9 percent or 3.0 percent.
The lower-than-expected growth in June was also due to technical reasons, said Mamoru Yamaguchi, an economist at Nikko Research Center.
"The month-end coincided with a weekend in June 1996, while the last day of June this year was a Monday. So the slower year-on-year growth may have been due to this technical factor," Yamaguchi said.

Weak demand for bank loans among big corporations and a cautious lending stance by banks towards non-manufacturers and small companies were behind the continuation of the slow growth in money supply, said Youchi Itoh, a senior economist at Daiwa Institute of Research.

"Banks, still suffering from bad loan problems, are unwilling to lend to smaller companies. They are willing to lend to bigger companies but big firms prefer to issue bonds to procure long-term funds," he said.
Itoh said he expects the year-on-year M2 plus CD growth rate to remain at slightly below three percent in the next few months.
